# Status (2026-11-02, evening)

**Question:** which insects traded **alive** online could be invasive plant pests in Norway (later the EU)?

**Scope rules**

- **Plant pests only:** insects, mites, land snails and slugs, apple snails (*Pomacea*) and nematodes. Crustaceans (e.g. *Eriocheir sinensis*), spiders, scorpions, ticks and marine or aquarium molluscs are out, even when EU-listed. Names with unknown class are kept and labelled.
- **Live specimens only:** dead material (pinned, papered, mounted, framed, ex-pupa specimens, collection, bodies, jewellery) is **labelled as dead, not deleted**. Unknown is kept.
- **Per species:** `live` if any live evidence; else `unknown` if any evidence of unclear form (human-food use, LEMIS unspecified); else `dead` if there is dead evidence; else `unknown`.
- **Food:** live feeders ("pet food", "feeder insects", "live food") count as **live**. Plain "food" (mostly human food) stays **unknown**, because the source doesn't say whether the insects were alive.
- **Regulated** = EPPO A1/A2, or any EU or Norwegian listing. A **whole-genus listing** (e.g. *Pomacea*) makes its species regulated when they have no EPPO code of their own. A genus match without a listing gives no credit.

| Step | Status |
|---|---|
| 1. Seed species list (Hughes 2026) | Done: 10,682 names (+420 live-imported LEMIS species = 11,102; 10,867 after merging synonyms) |
| 2. Collect live listings (NO/EU) | Shop scripts label each row live/dead/check/unknown and write to `5_outputs/tables/`. Norway sources not added yet |
| 3. Extract names from listings | Not started |
| 4. Resolve names (GBIF) | Done: 10,814 of 11,102 names resolved; 309 accepted species still have no class |
| 5. Pest lookup (EPPO) | Done: 814 species codes + 422 genus codes, local SQLite + GDAPI |
| 5b. Scope + life state | Done: LEMIS 2000–2022 (all forms), Lassaline use, Wang → `plant_pest_candidates.csv` (2,379) |
| 6. Tier A–D | Not started |
| 7. Pathway / FinnPRIO | Not started |

## Hughes et al. 2026 - wildlife trade data gaps
- *Sci. Adv.* 12:eaei3504, doi 10.1126/sciadv.aei3504. PDF: `Hughes_2026_wildlife_trade_data_gaps.pdf`.
- Supplementary data on figshare: https://doi.org/10.26188/33194898 (https://figshare.com/s/b05b15f87a58dd65eb1e)
- Title of dataset: "Appearance of species in trade data sources: Supplementary data for The true scale of global wildlife trade is obscured by data gaps"
- Also has a preprint on EcoEvoRxiv with supplementary files on Google Drive: https://ecoevorxiv.org/repository/view/11272/ (not downloaded; probably the same data).
- **Local:** `upSetData_singleNames_inv_comp.csv` (10,682 names) with 0/1 flags: CITES Trade, CITES App, LEMIS, LEMIS_noS, IUCN, TRAFFIC, Research. `Data_S1 - sourceSpeciesLists/` holds the raw lists per source.
- **Research flag** = the published studies they compiled: Lassaline 2025 (`inv_trim_1.csv`), Wang 2023 (`but_trim_1.csv`), Marshall 2022 (`ara_trim_1.csv`).
- **Limitation:** none of the flags say whether the animals were live or dead. `LEMIS = 1` covers any form, and 3,346 of the names flagged LEMIS have no live import record in 2000–2022.

## Lassaline et al. 2025 - global invertebrate trade
- *Biol. Conserv.* 308:111266, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biocon.2025.111266 (CC-BY). PDF: `Lassaline_2025_global_invertebrate_trade.pdf`.
- Data availability (from PDF): "The data supporting the findings of this study are available within the article and its supplementary materials."
- No external repository (Zenodo/figshare). The data is only in the supplementary appendix on ScienceDirect, downloaded by hand on 2026-11-02.
- Note: the figshare link 10.6084/m9.figshare.22115045 that appears in searches is for a DIFFERENT Lassaline paper (2023, Austral Entomology, "Untangling the web").
- **Local:** `mmc4.xlsx` holds 4,738 GBIF-resolved taxa with `reported_use` and source article. `mmc1`–`mmc3.docx` hold search terms and included/excluded literature.
- **Use → life state:** collection (3,410) = dead; pet (~1,030), pet food, biocontrol, pollination/honey, exhibit, aquarium = live; food (human), medical, venom = unknown.

## Wang et al. 2023 - butterfly species sold online
- *Biol. Conserv.* 283:110092, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biocon.2023.110092 (CC-BY). PDF: `Wang_2023_butterfly_species_sold_online.pdf`.
- Data availability (from PDF): "(1) All annotated butterfly transaction data; (2) species-level trait data used for price and volume predictions and (3) representative image clusters are deposited on Zenodo"
- Zenodo: https://zenodo.org/records/7825674 (README + **3** CSVs: SM1 species traits/volume/price, SM2 51,348 transactions 15.2 MB, SM3 image clusters). MD5 verified.
- GitHub (scraper code): https://github.com/Weilin37/ButterflyTradeEbay
- **Local:** SM2 covers all of 2022, eBay, with seller location. 873 sellers, names replaced by IDs. Top countries: DE, PL, GB, RU, US. **No Norwegian sellers.**
- **All dead:** titles say papered, unmounted, spread, framed, A1. "Ex pupa"/"ex larva" means reared and then mounted. Even the "larva" titles are mounted specimens or toy figures.

## Marshall et al. 2022 - arachnid trade
- *Commun. Biol.* 5:448, doi 10.1038/s42003-022-03374-0. PDF: `Marshall_2022_arachnid_trade.pdf`.
- Data availability (from PDF): "All data are available as supplements to this manuscript. Data used to produce figures and summary data are also available at [Zenodo]. Code used is available at [Zenodo]."
- Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5758540 and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5758541 point to the same 26 files (Data S1–S13, Code S01–S12). All downloaded, MD5 verified.
- Also on PMC: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9120460
- **Main value is the method:** Code S01–S05 (find sale websites with search engines, get the pages, build keywords from species names and synonyms, search the pages for them) is an R pipeline for step 2. Data S1 flags whether each website allows automated searching (useful for the terms-of-service question).

## LEMIS 2000–2022, corrected (Marshall et al. 2025)
- Marshall et al. 2025, "The magnitude of legal wildlife trade and implications for species survival", *PNAS* 122:e2410774121 (open access, PMC11745324).
- Data: figshare doi 10.6084/m9.figshare.25041584 (CC BY 4.0). Downloaded `lemisDataCorrected_2023-11-11.csv.gz` (230 MB), `MainDataFileDetails.txt`, `lemis_codes_2023-04-19.csv`, `nameConvertingKey_complete.csv`, `LEMIS_known_outliers.csv`. MD5 verified.
- Pre-2014 records are the Eskew et al. 2020 data. Names are corrected (`corrected`, `rank`), with a broad group (`group_`) and order. No company fields.
- A follow-up (Marshall et al. 2025, *Current Biology*, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.14982583) adds species distributions, but only for vertebrates and arachnids.
- Live codes: `LIV` live, `EGL` live eggs, `DEA` shipped live but died in transit; `UNS` = unspecified.
- **US imports only.** 8.7 M records; 963,710 live non-vertebrate import records; **1,323 species imported live**; 420 of them not in the Hughes list.
- Top live insects: *Drosophila melanogaster* (1,835 shipments), *Heliconius hecale*, *Morpho peleides* (1.09 M individuals), *H. melpomene*, *H. erato*, *Parides iphidamas*, mostly butterfly-house species from CR, EC, SV, KE, PH.
- **New compared with 2000–2014:** live imports of *Spodoptera frugiperda* (11,300 eggs from Brazil, 2017–2022, commercial/scientific), *Helicoverpa armigera* (3,000 + 3,000 eggs, AU/BR, biomedical/commercial), *Lycorma delicatula* (TH, 2021), *Diabrotica virgifera*, *Busseola fusca* (300 eggs, ZA), *Bagrada hilaris* (FR, scientific), and *Cydia pomonella* (157 shipments from Canada). These are lab or rearing supplies, not pet trade, but still live movement of pests.

## Older: LEMIS 2000–2014 (Eskew et al. 2020)
- github.com/eveskew/lemis release v1.1.0, `lemis.fst` (205 MB). `kephelps/LEMIS` on rdrr.io is a fork of the same package. Kept locally for reference, no longer used.

| Mites | 10 | 0 | 0 | 10 |

**Candidates** (in scope, live or unknown): **2,379**, in `5_outputs/tables/plant_pest_candidates.csv`. Of these, 27 are regulated (15 by their own species code, 12 *Pomacea* through the genus listing), and 11 of those have live evidence.

EPPO name matching (Hughes names): 753 exact, 32 synonym, 22 binomial-of-trinomial, 3 nominate subspecies (810 species codes, 627 insects); 2,953 genus only; 6,919 none.

## Findings so far
- **11 regulated plant pests are traded live.** Two different pathways:
  - **Pets:** ants (*Solenopsis invicta*, *S. geminata*, *Wasmannia auropunctata*, *Pachycondyla chinensis*) and apple snails (*Pomacea canaliculata*, *P. maculata*, *P. diffusa*). These match online pet trade, so ant-keeping and aquarium shops are the priority for step 2.
  - **Lab and rearing supply:** *Spodoptera frugiperda*, *Helicoverpa armigera*, *Lycorma delicatula*, *Diabrotica virgifera* (LEMIS 2015–2022, purposes commercial/scientific/biomedical). Probably not sold to hobbyists, but live movement all the same.
- **Most traded insects are dead:** 4,183 of 6,110 insect species have only dead evidence (eBay specimens, collections, LEMIS bodies). *Popillia japonica* and *Anoplophora* spp. appear only as dead material.
- **Live, plant-relevant, not regulated in NO/EU:** *Papilio demoleus*, *Cydia pomonella*, giant African snails (*Lissachatina fulica*, *Achatina achatina*), *Theba pisana*, *Cornu aspersum*, *Busseola fusca*, *Bagrada hilaris*, *Harmonia axyridis*, and many biocontrol agents (EPPO PM 6/3).
- **The newer LEMIS data matters:** 2015–2022 adds live imports of four regulated pests that 2000–2014 did not show.
- **Shops:** 546 unique shops found so far (710 rows); keyword labels give 256 live, 266 unknown, 13 dead and 11 check.
